case_number: CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2023 (@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRL.) NO.12216 OF 2022)

parties.respondent: The State of Karnataka and Another

summary: The appellants challenged the Karnataka High Court's judgment upholding their conviction under Section 304B, 498A r/w 34 IPC, and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, based primarily on a dying declaration. The prosecution alleged dowry harassment leading to the deceased's self-immolation. The Trial Court and High Court relied on the dying declaration (Ex.P.45) and medical testimony to affirm conviction. Appellants argued the deceased was physically and mentally incapacitated due to 70-80% burns and incapable of making a voluntary declaration. Multiple prosecution witnesses turned hostile. The Supreme Court evaluated the reliability of the dying declaration, considering medical evidence from PW-31 and PW-32, and the recording procedure by Tahsildar PW-25. It emphasized that a dying declaration can be sole basis for conviction if reliable and properly corroborated.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed. Conviction and sentence upheld.
